subject: Scaling path & renewal paperwork — addendum redlines needed
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearmap.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Scaling path & renewal paperwork

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our execs are aligned on moving forward with Redwood for another 12 months, but we need to bake in a short-term surge mechanism and a clearer addendum for the first-quarter capacity increase. I attached a draft addendum (Clearmap_Draft_Addendum_v3.docx) that our legal/procurement team pulled together. High-level asks: 

- Lock base term for 12 months (Jan 2027–Dec 2027)
- Add a defined “surge window” for up to 2x committed capacity for the first 90 days post-signature
- Define billing for surge (monthly true-up or overage at negotiated rate)
- Retain current SLA with a short carve-out for best-effort during surge windows

Can you and your team review, propose redlines, and confirm whether Redwood can support a pre-committed burst vs. pure on-demand? Procurement is cc’d (procurement@clearmap.ai); Markus Vogel will be the signer on their side.

Goal: have redlines and an updated order form back to us by EOD Tue (21 Dec) so procurement can prep DocuSign.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
CPO, Clearmap

(Attachment: Clearmap_Draft_Addendum_v3.docx)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearmap.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Scaling path & renewal paperwork

Alyssa — appreciate the clear ask and the draft. I’ve looped in Laura (Legal) and Priyom (Sales Ops) to scope the redlines and the order-form changes. Quick clarifying Qs before our redline pass: 

1) For the "2x committed capacity" in the first 90 days — is that relative to Clearmap’s current committed baseline (the 1.2M tokens/mo we have in the current order form)?
2) Do you want a separate pre-paid tranche for the surge, or would you prefer a committed burst with monthly reconciliation (true-up) at an agreed overage rate?
3) Any data residency or special audit language we should keep in the MSA addendum?

Proposed next steps: Laura will send the legal redlines tomorrow morning with suggested language for surge billing and an SLA carve-out. Priyom will update the order form capacity table and include a sample monthly true-up calculation so procurement has numbers for DocuSign. I’ll follow up once we have both artifacts.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through tradeoffs — say 10:30am PT?

Thanks — Michael
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: OrderForm_CapacityTable.xlsx - placeholder)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearmap.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Scaling path & renewal paperwork — redlines attached

Hi all —

I reviewed Clearmap_Draft_Addendum_v3 and attached a tracked-redline PDF (Redlines_MG_20261221.pdf) with commentary. Summary of key legal points and suggested language: 

- Term & Scope: We can agree to a 12-month renewal with an attached Addendum that defines the "Surge Period" as the first 90 days post-execution. I added explicit start/end dates so there’s no ambiguity.

- Surge capacity: Proposed two options (language added):
  A) Pre-committed burst: Customer prepays for an additional burst tranche (X tokens) at a discounted burst rate; unused burst capacity expires at the end of the Surge Period.
  B) Metered true-up: Provider supplies up to 2x baseline on-demand; usage above baseline is invoiced monthly at the agreed overage rate with a 30-day invoice dispute window.

- SLA carve-out: I inserted a narrow carve-out to our standard SLA for "performance degradation during Surge Periods where aggregate request volume exceeds baseline by >150% and is unanticipated." This limits credit exposure but preserves overall protections.

- Indemnity & Data: Maintained existing indemnity language; added a short sentence confirming no change to data residency or logging obligations.

- Order form linkage: I flagged several places where the Addendum must reference the specific Order Form line items and included a sample clause for capacity stacking and sequencing. 

Action items for Sales Ops (Priyom): please update the OrderForm_CapacityTable.xlsx with two rows: (1) base committed capacity (current baseline) and (2) surge tranche amounts and rates for both options (prepay & true-up). Also prepare a sample invoice calculation.

If we go with Option A (prepaid burst), Legal will require a short refund/expiry clause; Option B is operationally simpler but increases billing churn.

I’m comfortable with the overall structure but would like an explicit acceptance of the SLA carve-out from the customer.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Redlines_MG_20261221.pdf)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearmap.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Vogel <mvogel@clearmap.ai>, procurement@clearmap.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Scaling path & renewal paperwork — Clearmap preference

Laura / Michael —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear options. Clearmap’s preference is Option A (pre-committed burst) with the following specifics: 

- Burst tranche = 2x baseline for first 90 days (baseline = 1.2M tokens/mo), to be prepaid and available on demand.
- Any unused prepaid burst will expire at end of Surge Period; we accept that.
- Please include a monthly true-up only if usage exceeds prepaid + baseline for the period (i.e., overage scenario).
- We accept the SLA carve-out during the defined Surge Period as long as Redwood provides 24-hr advance notice for planned throttling and a point-of-contact for incident escalations.

Procurement next steps: Markus (cc’d) will confirm final signer and routing. His preference is DocuSign; please stage the combined packet (MSA + Addendum + updated Order Form) and send a DocuSign link to procurement@clearmap.ai and me once ready.

Targets: get packet to DocuSign by Thu 24 Dec so we have a chance to close before the holidays; if not, Jan 7 is acceptable.

Regards — Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
CPO, Clearmap

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearmap.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, Markus Vogel <mvogel@clearmap.ai>, procurement@clearmap.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Scaling path & renewal paperwork — final packet and next steps

Alyssa / Markus / Procurement —

Thanks — we’ll proceed with Option A (pre-committed burst) per Clearmap’s confirmation. Next steps and timeline: 

1) Priyom will finalize the OrderForm_CapacityTable.xlsx to show baseline, prepaid burst tranche (2x baseline for 90 days), pricing, and a sample invoice true-up calculation — target EOD today.
2) Laura will incorporate the agreed language (prepaid burst expiry, 24-hr notice for planned throttling, POC escalation path) into the Addendum and finalize the tracked clean copy.
3) I’ll assemble the combined packet (MSA + Addendum + updated Order Form) and route via DocuSign to procurement@clearmap.ai and Markus Vogel. Expect DocuSign envelope by Mon 27 Dec (holiday permitting); fallback signature target Jan 7, 2027.

Attaching the combined packet for your review (MG_Combined_Packet_20261223.pdf). Please confirm any last-minute edits by EOD Fri so we don’t delay the DocuSign.

Thanks for the partnership — looking forward to signing and getting you on the expanded path.

Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: MG_Combined_Packet_20261223.pdf, OrderForm_CapacityTable.xlsx)
